model selection is more effective in reducing the expected error of the SPODE ensemble, whereas model weighing is more effective in speeding up the classification process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in terms of classification accuracy, model weighing is superior to model selection, but in terms of computational time, model selection is superior to model weighing.
, in terms of accuracy and speed, model selection and model weighting are complementary to each other.
, in terms of classification accuracy, model weighing is generally more accurate than model selection; in terms of classification efficiency, model selection is generally faster than model weighing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best selection and weighing schemes depend on the underlying SPODEs' distributions, the number of candidate SPODE ensembles and the size of the training set.
model weighing can outperform model selection in terms of classification accuracy, while maintaining the efficiency advantage of SPODEs.
